__broaden__.αἰτιάασθαι: αἰτιάομαι — blame, find fault with; pres. inf. mid. dep., epic uncontracted -άασθαι (= Attic αἰτιᾶσθαι), after ἄνωγα · also pres. inf. mid. dep., after θυμός, of inclination: ’(your heart is set) to blame’
__broaden__.βίη: βίη — might, bodily strength, force; fem. nom. sg. · also periphrasis for a person, nom. subject: ’the might of Helenus’ (= Helenus himself)
__broaden__.εἶσι: εἶμι — go, come; pres. 3 sg. (neut. pl. subject with a sing. verb): ’go forth’ · also pres. 3 sg. with a fem. sg. subject: ’goes’
__broaden__.μάχην: μάχη — battle, fight; fem. acc. sg., object of καταδύμεναι: ’the fighting’ · also fem. acc. sg., after ἀνά (ἄν τε μάχην): ’through the fighting’ · also fem. acc. sg., object of ἐτάνυσσε: ’the fighting’ (μάχην ἐτάνυσσε ’stretched the battle’) · also fem. acc. sg., cognate object of ἐμάχοντο: ’fight’ (μάχην ἐμάχοντο ’fought the fight’) · also fem. acc. sg., object of ὄτρυνον: ’the fighting’ · also fem. acc. sg., with ἐς following it: ’into the battle’ (μάχην ἐς κυδιάνειραν ’into the man-glorifying battle’) · also fem. acc. sg., object of ἤγειρας: ’the battle’ (μάχην ἤγειρας ’you stirred up the battle’)
__broaden__.οἴω: ὀΐομαι — think, suppose; pres. 1 sg., act. form (= ὀΐω; Attic οἴομαι): ’I think’ · also οἶος — alone, only; masc. nom. dual οἴω, agreeing with the dual subject of οἴχεσθον: ’the two alone’
__broaden__.πολλὸς: πολύς — much, many, great; masc. nom. sg., epic πολλός (= Attic πολύς): ’huge’ of a body · also masc. nom. sg., of quantity, with χαλκός: ’much (bronze)’
__broaden__.πὰρ: παρά (apocope πάρ, grave before another word) — beside, alongside; prep. + dat.: ’beside’ · also prep. + acc., ’beside’ (πὰρ ποταμὸν ’beside the river’) · also prep. + gen., ’from beside’ (πὰρ Διὸς ’from Zeus’) · also adverb, ’beside him’ · also adverb, no case: ’beside, alongside’ (πὰρ δὲ … ἕστασαν ’and beside … stood’) · also prep. + gen., ’by, beside’ (πὰρ ποταμοῖο ’by the river’) · also prep. + acc., ’beyond’ (πὰρ δύναμιν ’beyond one’s power’)
__broaden__.πᾶσα: πᾶς — all, whole; fem. nom. sg., with χθών · also fem. nom. sg., agreeing with ἔπαλξις: ’the whole (of it)’ · also fem. nom. sg., agreeing with Ἴλιος: ’all (of Ilios)’
__broaden__.υἷ: υἱός — son; masc. acc. sg., elided (υἷ’ = υἷα, epic for Attic υἱόν) · also υἷε, masc. acc. dual, elided (υἷ’ = υἷε): ’the two sons’
__broaden__.φθαίη: φθάνω — be first, get ahead; aor. opt. 3 sg. (ἔφθην), in a purpose clause after ἵνα μή, + part.: ’might be first (to vaunt)’ · also aor. opt. 3 sg. with κε, potential: ’would be first (to be taken)’
__broaden__.ἀνάλκιδα: ἄναλκις — without strength, unwarlike, cowardly; masc. acc. sg., agreeing with σε: ’a coward’ · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with ἐμέ: ’(me) without might’
__broaden__.ἄκρης: ἄκρος — topmost, high; adj., fem. gen. sg., Ionic -ης (= Attic -ᾱς), agreeing with πόλιος: ’of the high (city)’ · also fem. gen. sg., agreeing with Περγάμου: ’high’ (κατὰ Περγάμου ἄκρης ’down from high Pergamos’) (or the noun ἄκρη ’height’, with Περγάμου depending on it) · also fem. gen. sg. in κατ’ ἄκρης, with no noun expressed: ’from the top down, utterly’
__broaden__.ἐπειρᾶτο: πειράω — try, attempt; mid. impf. 3 sg., + inf.: ’tried (to)’ · also absolute, with an εἰ-clause: ’made trial (whether)’
__broaden__.ἐρύκακε: ἐρύκω — hold back, ward off; aor. 3 sg., epic reduplicated aorist: ’held off’ · also aor. imper. 2 sg., epic reduplicated: ’hold back!’
__broaden__.ἐσσύμενον: σεύω — drive, hurry (mid. rush, hasten); perf. part. mid./pass. masc. acc. sg., epic doubled σ, agreeing with σε: ’hurrying’ · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with Ἕκτορα: ’eager for (war)’ (ἐσσύμενον πολέμοιο ’eager for battle’) · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with an understood subject of an infinitive: ’(one) eager’
__broaden__.ἔκλυον: κλύω — hear, hearken to (+ gen.); aor. 3 pl. (also 1 sg.), in a general statement: ’they hear’ · also aor. 1 sg. + gen. of the speaker: ’I heard (it from one who told it)’ · also aor. 3 pl. + acc. of what is heard, in plain narrative: ’they heard’ (Ἕκτορος … αὐδήν ’Hector’s voice’)
__broaden__.ἔμενον: μένω — wait, stand firm; impf. 3 pl.: ’stood their ground’ · also impf. 3 pl. + acc. of what is awaited: ’awaited’

αἰθέρα: αἰθήρ — upper air, bright sky; masc. acc. sg.
αἰπεινή: αἰπεινός — steep, sheer, lofty (poetic by-form of αἰπύς); fem. nom. sg., agreeing with the city name Ἴλιος
αὐγάς: αὐγή — light, gleam, glare; fem. acc. pl.
βιβάσθων: βιβάω (βίβημι) — stride, step; pres. part. act. masc. nom. sg., lengthened -άσθων (cf. βιβάς): ’taking long strides’
βουγάϊε: βουγάϊος — braggart (a guess; meaning not known); masc. voc. sg., a term of abuse
δάψει: δάπτω — tear, rend, devour; fut. 3 sg. act.: ’will tear’
δακρυοέσσης: δακρυόεις — tearful, full of tears; fem. gen. sg., epic -οέσσης (the feminine of the -όεις adjectives)
δειδίσσεαι: δειδίσσομαι — frighten, terrify; pres. 2 sg. mid. dep., epic uncontracted -εαι (= Attic -ῃ), active sense: ’you frighten’
δεξιὸς: δεξιός — right, on the right, auspicious; masc. nom. sg., agreeing with ὄρνις: ’on the right’ (the lucky side for an omen)
δευήσεσθαι: δεύομαι — lack, be in want of (+ gen.); fut. inf. mid., epic (cf. Attic δεήσεσθαι from δέομαι)
δηΐφοβός: Δηΐφοβος — Deiphobus, a son of Priam, a Trojan warrior; masc. nom. sg.
δύναμιν: δύναμις — power, might, ability; fem. acc. sg.
εἰπόντι: εἶπον — say, speak; aor. part. act., masc. dat. sg., agreeing with οἱ: ’to him as he spoke’
εἴξειαν: εἴκω — yield, give way (+ dat.); aor. opt. 3 pl. act., after εἴ πώς: ’they might yield’
θάρσυνος: θάρσυνος — bold, confident, emboldened; adj., masc. nom. sg., with a dat. of cause: ’emboldened by’
θάσσονας: θάσσων — swifter (comparative of ταχύς); masc. acc. pl., epic θάσσων (= Attic θάττων)
θαρσύνονθ: θαρσύνω — encourage, cheer; pres. part. act. masc. acc. sg., elided and aspirated (θαρσύνονθ’ = θαρσύνοντα), epic (= Attic θαρρύνω)
θεσπεσίῳ: θεσπέσιος — wondrous, divine, beyond mortal scale; masc. dat. sg., agreeing with ὁμάδῳ
κέατο: κεῖμαι — lie, lie dead; impf. 3 pl. mid. dep., epic κέατο (= Attic ἔκειντο): ’lay’
κονίοντες: κονίω — raise dust, cover with dust; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’raising the dust’
κορέεις: κορέννυμι — sate, glut; fut. 2 sg. act., epic uncontracted and without σ (= Attic κορέσεις): ’you will sate’
κροτάφοισι: κρόταφος — temple (of the head); masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις); plural for the two temples
κυρτὰ: κυρτός — curved, arched, bulging; neut. nom. pl., agreeing with κύματα
λάθοντο: λανθάνομαι (λήθομαι) — forget (+ gen.); aor. 3 pl. mid., epic unaugmented (= Attic ἐπελάθοντο): ’they forgot’
λειριόεντα: λειριόεις — lily-like, delicate (λείριον ’lily’; exact sense uncertain); masc. acc. sg., agreeing with χρόα
μέλλω: μέλλω — be about to, intend, be likely to; pres. 1 sg. + inf.: ’I am about to, I am set to’
μίσγεται: μίσγω — mix, mingle; pres. mid./pass. 3 sg. + dat.: ’mingles with’
μακρῇσι: μακρός — long; fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσι (= Attic -αις)
μαρμαίροντες: μαρμαίρω — flash, gleam, sparkle; pres. part. act. masc. nom. pl.: ’gleaming’
μόρυν: Μόρυς — Morys, a Phrygian ally of Troy, son of Hippotion; masc. acc. sg.
ναιομένη: ναίω — dwell, inhabit; pres. part. mid./pass. fem. nom. sg.: ’inhabited’
νιφόεντι: νιφόεις — snowy, snow-clad (νίφω ’snow’); neut. dat. sg., epic -όεις, agreeing with ὄρεϊ
οἰωνῷ: οἰωνός — bird of prey; bird of omen, omen; masc. dat. sg., of cause: ’by the omen’
οἴσουσι: φέρω (fut. stem οἰσ-) — carry, bear; fut. 3 pl.: ’they will carry’
οἴχεσθον: οἴχομαι — be gone, have gone, depart; pres. 3 dual mid. dep. (same form as 2 dual), with perfect sense: ’the two are gone’
πάλμύν: Πάλμυς — Palmys, a Trojan ally; masc. acc. sg. (printed with an acute on -ύν)
πέδον: πέδον — ground, earth; neut. acc. sg., of the goal with -δε (πέδον δέ ’to the ground’)
πέτετ: πέτομαι — fly, speed; impf. 3 sg. mid. dep., elided and unaugmented (πέτετ’ = ἐπέτετο): ’flew, sped’
πήληξ: πήληξ — helmet, crest-bearing helmet; fem. nom. sg.
πανθοΐδην: Πανθοΐδης — son of Panthous, patronymic (of Polydamas); masc. acc. sg.
παφλάζοντα: παφλάζω — bubble, seethe, splutter; pres. part. act. neut. nom. pl., agreeing with κύματα: ’seething’
πεφήσεαι: φένω (aor. ἔπεφνον) — slay; fut. 2 sg. pass. of the reduplicated stem πεφη-, epic uncontracted -εαι (= Attic -ῃ): ’you will be slain’
πολυφήτην: Πολυφήτης — Polyphetes, a Phrygian ally of Troy; masc. acc. sg.
προβιβῶντι: προβιβάω — step forward, stride on; pres. part. act. masc. dat. sg., contracted (= προβιβάοντι): ’as he strides forward’
προμάχους: πρόμαχος — front-fighter, champion; masc. acc. pl.
προτέρῃ: πρότερος — before, earlier, former; fem. dat. sg., Ionic -ῃ (= Attic -ᾳ), agreeing with ἠοῖ: ’on the earlier (dawn)’
πρυμνῇσιν: πρυμνός (or noun πρύμνη) — hindmost, the stern; fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσιν (= Attic -αις); adjective or noun, parse uncertain: ’at the sterns’
πυκινήν: πυκινός — close-packed, solid, stout; fem. acc. sg., epic πυκινός (= Attic πυκνός), agreeing with ἀσπίδα
σείετο: σείω — shake, brandish; impf. 3 sg. mid./pass., epic unaugmented (= ἐσείετο): ’was shaken’
σῶς: σῶς (epic σάος) — safe, sound; also ’sure, certain’; masc. nom. sg., agreeing with ὄλεθρος: ’sure’
τέκοι: τίκτω — bear, give birth to; aor. opt. 3 sg. act., in a wish: ’may she have borne’
ταλάσσῃς: ταλάω (τλάω) — bear, endure, bring oneself to; aor. subj. 2 sg. act., epic -σσ-, with inf.: ’you bring yourself (to)’
τείχει: τεῖχος — wall, rampart; neut. dat. sg. (contracted from -εϊ)
τετυμμένω: τύπτω — strike, wound; perf. part. mid./pass. masc. nom. dual: ’(the two) struck’
φάλκην: Φάλκης — Phalces, a Trojan ally; masc. acc. sg.
φαεινὴ: φαεινός — shining, bright (φάος ’light’), a poetic word; fem. nom. sg., agreeing with πήληξ
φαληριόωντα: φαληριάω — gleam white, be flecked with foam; pres. part. neut. nom. pl., epic uncontracted -ιόωντα (= -ιῶντα), agreeing with κύματα
ἀγαπήνορα: ἀγαπήνωρ — man-cherishing, loving manliness (exact sense not known); masc. acc. sg., epithet of a hero
ἀδάμας: Ἀδάμας — Adamas, a Trojan, son of Asius; masc. nom. sg.
ἀδαήμονές: ἀδαήμων — unversed in, ignorant of (+ gen.); masc. nom. pl.
ἀμοιβοὶ: ἀμοιβός — in exchange, in turn; as noun, a replacement, relief; masc. nom. pl., in apposition to the subject: ’as replacements’
ἀνολέθρους: ἀνώλεθρος — unharmed, undestroyed (ἀν- + ὄλεθρος); masc. acc. pl., epic ἀνολέθρους (= Attic ἀνωλέθρους)
ἀπήμονας: ἀπήμων — unharmed, free from harm; masc. acc. pl.
ἀρήσῃ: ἀράομαι — pray (to); aor. subj. 2 sg. mid. dep., after ὁππότε: ’you will pray’, + dat. of the god
ἀργαλέων: ἀργαλέος — grievous, harsh, troublesome; masc. gen. pl.
ἀρηρότες: ἀραρίσκω — fit together, join; perf. part. masc. nom. pl., intransitive: ’ranged closely, fitted’
ἀσιάδης: Ἀσιάδης — son of Asius, patronymic (of Adamas); masc. nom. sg.
ἀσκάνιόν: Ἀσκάνιος — Ascanius, a Phrygian ally of Troy, son of Hippotion; masc. acc. sg., accent from the enclitic τε
ἁλὶ: ἅλς — sea, salt water; fem. dat. sg.
ἁμαρτοεπὲς: ἁμαρτοεπής — errant in speech, speaking wide of the mark (ἁμαρτάνω + ἔπος); adj., masc. voc. sg., in address
ἄρχ: ἄρχω — begin, lead the way (+ gen.); pres. imper. 2 sg. act., elided (ἄρχ’ = ἄρχε): ’lead on!’
ἐγχείῃσιν: ἐγχείη — spear; fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσιν (= Attic -αις), instrumental
ἐδάμημεν: δάμνημι (δαμάζω) — subdue, overpower; aor. pass. 1 pl., epic (= Attic ἐδαμάσθημεν): ’we were overcome’
ἐλθέ: ἔρχομαι — come, go; aor. imper. 2 sg. (aor. stem ἐλθ-, accented ἐλθέ): ’come!’
ἐμμεμαῶτες: ἐμμέμαα (μάω) — strive, be eager; perf. part. masc. nom. pl., epic -ῶτες (Attic -ότες): ’eager’
ἐξαλαπάξειν: ἐξαλαπάζω — sack utterly, plunder; fut. inf. act., after ἐέλπεται: ’to plunder utterly’
ἐπέπτατο: ἐπιπέτομαι — fly at, fly up to; aor. 3 sg. mid. (ἐπί + ἔπτατο, aorist of πέτομαι): ’flew up’
ἐπελήλατο: ἐπελαύνω (ἐλάω) — drive on, hammer on; plpf. 3 sg. mid./pass., with reduplication ἐλήλα-: ’had been driven on, laid on’
ἐπεσσεύοντ: ἐπισεύομαι (σεύω) — rush on, hurry to; impf. 3 pl. mid., epic doubled σ, elided (ἐπεσσεύοντ’ = ἐπεσσεύοντο): ’rushed up’
ἐπιόντας: ἔπειμι (ἐπί + εἶμι) — come on, advance, approach; pres. part. act. masc. acc. pl.: ’advancing’
ἐποτρύνοντα: ἐποτρύνω — urge on, stir up; pres. part. act. masc. acc. sg., + inf.: ’urging on (to fight)’
ἐρωῆσαι: ἐρωέω — draw back, hold back, rest (+ gen. of what one leaves); aor. inf. act., after μέλλω: ’to hold back (from)’
ἑλένοιο: Ἕλενος — Helenus, a son of Priam, a seer; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ἑψόμεθ: ἕπομαι — follow; fut. 1 pl. mid., elided (ἑψόμεθα): ’we shall follow’
ἠχὴ: ἠχή — sound, din, roar; fem. nom. sg.
ἤγειρας: ἐγείρω — rouse, wake, stir up; aor. 2 sg. act., augmented: ’you roused’
ἰρήκων: ἴρηξ (Attic ἱέραξ) — hawk; masc. gen. pl., of comparison after a comparative: ’than hawks’
ἱπποτίωνος: Ἱπποτίων — Hippotion, father of Ascanius and Morys; masc. gen. sg.
ὀθρυονεύς: Ὀθρυονεύς — Othryoneus, a Trojan ally; masc. nom. sg.
ὀλέσαντες: ὄλλυμι — destroy, lose; aor. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’having lost’
ὀρθαῖόν: Ὀρθαῖος — Orthaeus, a Phrygian ally of Troy; masc. acc. sg., accent from the enclitic τε
ὁμάδῳ: ὅμαδος — din, uproar, noise of a crowd; masc. dat. sg., of manner: ’with a roar’
ὄρεϊ: ὄρος — mountain; neut. dat. sg., epic ὄρεϊ (= Attic ὄρει), after ἐοικώς
ὑμὴ: ὑμός — your (pl.), yours; possessive adj., fem. nom. sg., epic/Ionic (= Attic ὑμετέρα), agreeing with πόλις
ὑρτάκου: Ὕρτακος — Hyrtacus, father of Asius; masc. gen. sg.
ῥινοῖσιν: ῥινός — hide, skin (of an ox); fem. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οῖς), of material: ’with hides’
